transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; what brings you in to see me today?

Hey, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in because... ever since I moved into this busted-up room I'm renting, things have just been off. I’m snapping at people a lot. I end up staying up half the night just trying to fix leaks or get the heat working, and then... I just drag myself in late to work. And lately I'm messing up stuff on the job site that I normally handle without a problem. I just need to figure out how to get a handle on it.

Do you feel like these feelings of being 'off' and struggling at work happen only when you are dealing with the problems in your room, or do they persist even when you are away from the apartment and trying to relax?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't really thought about it like that. I guess... it just kind of feels like it's always hanging over me right now. Even when I leave the apartment and try to just grab a beer or chill out somewhere else, I'm still just... wound up about the whole thing. So I don't really know if it ever completely shuts off.
How long have you been living in this apartment, and did you feel like yourself before you moved in?

Yeah, I felt like myself before. I was doing pretty normal before I moved into that room. I haven't been there too long, but... well, this all really started within the first couple weeks of moving in, right after I found the water damage and realized the heat was messed up. That's when things just started going downhill.

When you feel wound up, are your worries specifically about the situation with your apartment, or do you find yourself feeling just as anxious about other things, like your job performance, your finances, or your health in general?

I don't really think about that other stuff. It's... it's pretty much just the apartment. I mean, I'm not sitting around worrying about my health or anything like that. 

I guess I'm a little stressed about my job right now, but that's only because I'm screwing up since I'm so tired from dealing with the room. But nah, it's not like I'm just worried about everything in general. It all just goes back to that place.
Beyond feeling wound up and stressed, have you been feeling down, hopeless, or like you've lost interest in things you usually enjoy since moving in?

Not really, no. I mean... I wouldn't say I feel hopeless or down in the dumps. I'm just really frustrated and tired. I still like doing the stuff I normally do, I just... well, I'm usually too worn out or annoyed about the apartment to actually go do it right now. But nah, it's not like I've lost interest or feel depressed.
Have you found yourself acting out, being reckless, or perhaps getting into any arguments or confrontations with others beyond just snapping at them since you moved in?

No, I haven't been doing anything reckless or getting into fights or anything like that. I mean, I'm definitely irritable, like I said, and I might snap at someone if they catch me at a bad time, but I'm not out there acting crazy or picking fights. I just go to work, come back, and try to deal with the apartment. That's pretty much it.
When you are feeling 'wound up' about the apartment, does it feel more like a sense of nervousness, tension, or worry, or does it feel more like a sense of sadness or tearfulness?

Definitely the tension and worry. I'm not sitting around crying or feeling sad about it. It's just... I get all tense, like I can't relax my muscles after work. I'm just constantly worried about having to deal with the place. So yeah, no sadness or tearfulness or anything like that, just feeling really stressed and on edge.
When you feel that tension and worry, do you often find yourself feeling physically restless, like you can't sit still or need to keep moving?

Not really, no. I don't feel like I need to keep moving or anything. Honestly, after being on a job site all day, I usually just want to sit down. 

My muscles stay tight, like I said, but I'm not pacing around or feeling restless. I can sit still fine... I just can't actually relax while I'm doing it.
Even if you don't feel 'down' or 'sad,' have you noticed any changes in your appetite or how much you are eating since this started?

No, my appetite is pretty much the same. I still eat normally. I mean, doing construction, I burn a lot of energy, so I still get hungry and eat what I usually do. I haven't noticed any changes there.
Have you found yourself wanting to avoid your friends or social activities more than usual since this started, even if you don't feel 'sad'?

No, not really. I still see my friends. I mean, we still grab a beer after work or hang out on the weekends like we usually do. I haven't been avoiding anyone or staying home more than normal. I'm still doing all my regular stuff, just... you know, with all this apartment stress on my mind. But yeah, I'm not dodging my buddies or anything.
Even though you mentioned you aren't feeling 'down' or crying, have you noticed that you've been feeling unusually irritable, moody, or having a 'short fuse' more than you typically would?

Yeah, actually, I have been. That's kind of why I'm here. Ever since I moved into that busted-up apartment, I've had a really short fuse. I'm snapping at people a lot more than I usually would. And... well, I'm staying up late trying to fix leaks or deal with the heat not working, so I end up dragging myself into work late. Then, because I'm so tired and stressed, I'm messing up stuff on the job site that I normally handle with no problem. So, yeah, I've definitely been more irritable.
Even though you feel like you're still doing your regular activities, have you noticed that those things don't feel quite as enjoyable or rewarding as they did before you moved?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I mean, when I'm out grabbing a beer with the guys or watching a game, I'm still having a good time. It's not like I stopped liking the stuff I usually do. It's just... I guess the stress is always waiting for me when I get back to that apartment, so it's on my mind a lot. But yeah, the fun stuff is still fun for me.
Since moving in, have you noticed that you feel noticeably slower in your movements or that your thinking feels more sluggish than it did before?

No, not really. I mean, I'm tired from being up late dealing with the apartment, but I wouldn't say I'm moving slower or having a hard time thinking. I'm just exhausted, you know? But my head works fine, and I'm moving around the job site same as always, just... maybe a little heavier from lack of sleep. But not sluggish like that.
Have you noticed that you've been feeling unusually empty, numb, or just lacking in any positive emotion since this started?

No, not empty or numb. I mean, like I said a minute ago, I still have a good time and laugh when I'm out with the guys. I definitely still have positive emotions. It's really just the stress and being pissed off about the apartment that's getting to me. I don't feel hollowed out or anything like that.
Even though you still find your usual activities enjoyable, have you noticed that you are finding it harder to get motivated to actually start doing them compared to before you moved?

No, I wouldn't say that. If anything, I'm more motivated to get out and do stuff just so I don't have to be in that apartment. When the guys ask if I want to go grab a drink or do something, I'm pretty quick to say yes. It gets me out of the house, so getting started isn't a problem at all.
Do you find that you've been feeling more discouraged or pessimistic about your future or your ability to solve this housing situation than you felt before you moved?

No, I don't think so. I mean, it sucks right now, and I'm really frustrated with the landlord, but I don't feel like it's hopeless or anything. I know I'll figure it out eventually, whether I get him to fix the place or I just pack up and find somewhere else to live. I'm not... I'm not sitting around thinking my life is ruined or that things won't get better. It's just a massive headache right now, that's all.

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about feelings of emptiness, numbness, or a lack of positive emotion (anhedonia/depressive symptoms). None of the items in my symptom profile cover these specific emotional symptoms.

patient.answer: No, not empty or numb. I mean, like I said a minute ago, I still have a good time and laugh when I'm out with the guys. I definitely still have positive emotions. It's really just the stress and being pissed off about the apartment that's getting to me. I don't feel hollowed out or anything like that.

doctor.intent: Distinguish between F43.22 (Adjustment disorder with anxiety) and F43.23 (Adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood) by checking for specific, subtle signs of depressive affect or lack of pleasure, even if the patient claims to enjoy activities.
doctor.question: Even though you still find your usual activities enjoyable, have you noticed that you are finding it harder to get motivated to actually start doing them compared to before you moved?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a decrease in motivation to initiate activities (avolition/apathy), which is not covered by any of the items in my symptom profile.

patient.answer: No, I wouldn't say that. If anything, I'm more motivated to get out and do stuff just so I don't have to be in that apartment. When the guys ask if I want to go grab a drink or do something, I'm pretty quick to say yes. It gets me out of the house, so getting started isn't a problem at all.

doctor.intent: Distinguish between F43.22 (Adjustment disorder with anxiety) and F43.23 (Adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood) by checking for specific, though perhaps mild, emotional symptoms of depression that the patient might not have identified as 'sadness'.
doctor.question: Do you find that you've been feeling more discouraged or pessimistic about your future or your ability to solve this housing situation than you felt before you moved?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about feelings of hopelessness, discouragement, or pessimism regarding the future (a symptom of depression). The patient's symptom profile does not include a specific item for hopelessness or pessimism.

patient.answer: No, I don't think so. I mean, it sucks right now, and I'm really frustrated with the landlord, but I don't feel like it's hopeless or anything. I know I'll figure it out eventually, whether I get him to fix the place or I just pack up and find somewhere else to live. I'm not... I'm not sitting around thinking my life is ruined or that things won't get better. It's just a massive headache right now, that's all.

inference.note: The patient's symptoms (irritability, tension, and sleep disturbance) clearly point toward an adjustment disorder. The lack of depressed mood or feelings of hopelessness effectively rules out F43.23 (adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood).
